newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields rise to 18.93 pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela 6-month TEM yields rise to 18.93 pct.

text.p: Yields on Venezuelan benchmark six-month TEMs rose 12 basis points to 18.93 percent in Wednesday's auction, according to a calculation by Reuters that uses the Central Bank formula.

The Central Bank said it sold 60 billion bolivars of 178- day "monetary stabilization", or TEM, bills with a 18.81 percent coupon for a price of 99.95 pct. At last week's auction the six month notes yielded 18.81 percent

The bank also sold 20 billion bolivars of 267-day notes with a 19.24 percent coupon at a price of 99.30 percent, and 20 billion bolivars of 358-day notes with a 19.70 percent coupon at an average price of 98.89 percent.
Yields for the 267-day notes rose 60 basis points to 20.33 percent, but fell 20 basis points to 21.05 percent for the 358- day TEMs.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
